greetings.h:
Office of International and Public Affairs

GIST have built our current reputation through reaching beyond the borders of Korea and competing on an international scale.

GIST is a proud creator of future science and technology, as our motto says. We believe that the quality of research done here is on par with that of the global top-tier universities. We have built our current reputation through reaching beyond the borders of Korea and competing on an international scale.

Due to adapting to a new culture and environment, studying abroad can be difficult for students. However, at GIST we give our international students the respect and encouragement they need to face these challenges.

In the QS World University Rankings announced in 2023, GIST was No. 6 in the world and No. 1 in Korea in the category of citations per faculty. This is considered an important index for evaluating a school’s research performance, with more citations indicating better research quality.

GIST also launched its undergraduate program in March 2010. With the graduation of this inaugural college class, GIST is expected to make an impressive entrance into overall university rankings as well.

About one-tenth of the current student body is composed of international students. We will be there to advise and guide you so that you can successfully complete your tasks.

We look forward to having you join us. You will receive a great education and help GIST continue to grow as a highly competitive international campus.

IPA’s door is always wide open.

Thank you.

Chang-duk Jun Dean of Section of International and Public Affairs

gip.h:
For those of you who would like to experience the unique research environment and opportunities available at the GIST, the Global Intern Program (GIP) offers a wonderful opportunity to experience research at GIST by having you join a research lab for eight-weeks during the summer to receive valuable training and mentoring from the lab's professor. It will be an opportunity to help you decide if pursuing an advanced degree at GIST is right for you while gaining valuable research experience.

Eligibility for Applicants

  • International Undergraduate Seniors or Master's Degree students
  • GPA (Grade Point Average) of 3.0 or above (on a 4.5 point scale) or equivalent
  • TOEFL iBT 80 or its equivalent on another English Language Proficiency test
    *If the students' nationality is from an English-speaking country or the medium of instruction at their home university is English, they can submit a passport copy or a certificate stating "Medium of Instruction is English" instead of an English language proficiency test score.

inbound-exchange.h:
Who can apply?

Students from one of our partner institutions who meet the exchange eligibility requirements may apply. These requirements may vary for different institutions, so please contact your international student exchange coordinator for details about the eligibility requirements.

Depending on the institutional agreement, eligible students may study for one or two semesters at GIST. Tuition fees are to be paid to your home university. If you wish to study at GIST as an exchange student, please contact the exchange coordinator at your home institution for details about the selection process, such as eligibility, required documents, and deadlines.

Students should check with their home institution coordinator to verify that GIST is a partner institution with your home institution.

GIST will only process applicants who have been approved by their home institution to apply for the GIST Student Exchange Program.

Application Requirements

To apply for the Inbound Exchange Program, you must satisfy the following criteria

  • Minimum 1 year of full-time study at year home institution
  • Grade Point Average (GPA) of 3.0 or better (on a 4.5 point scale) or equivalent
  • TOEFL iBT 80 or its equivalent on another English language proficiency test

Initial Contact by Your Home Institution

Your home institution coordinator must notify GIST by email at mobility@gist.ac.kr that you have been approved by your home institution to apply for the GIST Student Exchange Program. Your home institution coordinator should also provide GIST with the following information: your full name, major/concentration, degree program, year of study, GPA, and English proficiency test results.

outbound.h:
GIST Outbound Programs

One foundation of an exciting liberal arts education is to expose students to the global diversity of human culture and traditions, and GIST is here to help students gain these valuable experiences through our GIST Outbound Programs. These varied and dynamic programs give GIST students an unparalleled opportunity to develop their global awareness, intercultural understanding, and stronger language skills by studying abroad for a semester in another country.

Besides experiencing new and challenging academic opportunities, studying abroad in another country will give GIST students the chance to immerse themselves in another culture and environment that will further expand their understanding and appreciation of the world where we all live.

GIST has established Outbound Programs with prestigious institutions across the world, and students should take full advantage of these opportunities to enrich their lives and their studies.

For those who are ready to start a new and challenging adventure, GIST encourages qualified students to apply and embark on an intellectually rewarding journey to explore the world outside of Korea through our GIST Outbound Programs.

Learn more about these exciting opportunities now!

outbound-exchange.h:
Outbound Exchange (Mobility Program)

Choose your institution based on your academic needs and requirements. Because some institutions only accept students from a particular department or concentration, please check our partner institutions’ websites to ensure that your planned course of study is suitable. Also, please consult your GIST course catalogue to determine what courses and electives would be appropriate for you to take at the overseas institution.

To determine if courses satisfy GIST's requirements, consult the GIST professor in charge of your designated concentration after thoroughly reviewing our partner institutions' websites.

Based on a review and assessment of the course content, the dean of your department will make the final decision on how many credits you will receive for each course you take at the overseas institution.

For further inquiries, please contact the Section of Student Records (T.2053)

Eligibility

As a GIST student you can study for one or two semesters at an overseas university and earn credit towards your degree through the GIST Student Mobility Program.

  • Eligibility Requirements
    • Current enrollment in a degree program at GIST
    • Undergraduate students must have completed at least two semesters before applying
    • Cumulative GPA of at least 3.0 in your current GIST courses
    • Meets the requirements of the host university
    • At least one semester left to complete upon returning to GIST
    • Students must pay tuition fees to the home institution for the dispatch semester and maintain the enrolled status.
    • Ability to be financially self-sufficient for the exchange period. Tuition fees at the host institution are waived, but students are required to pay travel and living expenses. The ideal time to go on exchange is during your second semester of your second year, or first semester of your third year (as an undergraduate).
  • Many of GIST's exchange agreements are for undergraduate students only.
  • Please refer to our list of Partner Institutions.
  • If you require more information about partner institutions, or want to consult with the coordinator, please visit the Section of Public Affaris, located on the 3rd floor of the Administraion building (S2).
    • Monday ~ Friday
    • 9 A.M. ~ 6 P.M.
    • +82-62-715-6257

outbound-exchange-scholarship.h:
GIST Scholarship

GIST Students who participate in the Mobility Program may be eligible to receive additional scholarships or financial assistance from GIST. The amount will be determined on a case-by-case basis and will depend on a country where the dispatched university is located at.

Mirrae Asset Scholarship

The Mirrae Asset Student Exchange Scholarship Program started in 2008 to fund students' study abroad opportunities so that they can experience different cultures to help them become global leaders in the future.

Selection Criteria & Application Requirements

GIST students need to be selected by their school or department. Please check the GIST International and Public Affairs website for more information as well as the Mirae Asset Scholarship Homepage (http://foundation.miraeasset.com) because the selection criteria changes every semester.

ASEM-Duo Scholarship Program

ASEM member countries form an exchange pair (Europe-Asia) between institutions. During the exchange, scholarships are provided through this program. ASEM-Duo offers scholarships for: Duo-Korea, Duo-France, and Duo-Singapore.

Which exchanges between countries qualify for this scholarship?

This is an exchange between ASEM member countries, so the applicant must check if their country is a member of ASEM. (There are 25 ASEM member countries: Greece, Denmark, Belgium, France, Finland, Germany, England, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, Ireland, Austria, China, Japan, Korea, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Vietnam, and Brunei.) Duo-Korea exchanges with European ASEM member countries. Those applying through Duo-Korea must be affiliated with a Korean educational institution and must find a pair amongst one of the European ASEM member countries. If a European ASEM member country wishes to exchange with Korea, the Korean educational institution must find its pair, and then the applicant may apply to Duo-Korea through the Korean institution. But, a formal exchange agreement must exist between the Korean and European educational institutions. Scholarships will be provided to both students when selected. When forming pairs, the candidates must be of the same category (i.e. student-student).

A student is defined as an individual enrolled in an degree program (undergraduate, masters, or Ph.D.) at an accredited educational institution.

Who can apply?

There are minor differences between programs. Current undergraduates, graduate students, and professors may participate in this program.

How can I apply?

The GIST Section of Public Affairs will inform you of the documents needed once the possibility of the 1:1 exchange with the European sister school has been confirmed. Students must then fill out an application and submit necessary documents to the International Relations Team.

Do all applicants receive scholarships?

No, because The ASEM-Duo Scholarship Foundation determines qualifications and eligibility of scholarship recipients.

For more information please refer to the ASEM-Duo Korea website: http://www.asemduo.org
